utterances.text: Perhaps if you could go to P 00391, just as a different process, this concerns a meeting that was held in -- according to the top of the document, and I apologise, it's getting late in the day, these are minutes from a meeting in Grude on the 14th of August, 1992. And when we look at the persons in attendance there seem to be people from many parts of Central Bosnia, Gornji Vakuf, number 13; number 15, Novi Travnik; number 22, a man from Vares; number 29, Dario Kordic from Busovaca; number 30, three men from Sarajevo; et cetera; Perica Jukic from Central Bosnia HVO. It appears to indicate, does it not, that these people were able to travel to Grude for purposes of this meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there, but they probably did get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm not trying to force anything on to you. I'm just saying that that's what the document would appear to indicate, doesn't it? Taking the document on face value.

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, they either went there or they were there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you could look at one -- in the same binder and there's also a mixture of P and D, but if you can please find 1D 01182, I believe this is a document we've seen in the courtroom before, 1D 01182. It's probably well down into the binder. I also had trouble finding that one, sir, I'm sorry. All right. On the e-court, thank you. Again, sir, this appears to be a document of minutes of a meeting on the 27th of February, 1993, and just as an example I think if you go down to paragraph number 4 of the document -- paragraph numbered 4, it's at the bottom of the page 2 in the English, I'm not sure about the -- let me see. Either number -- you have it there, page 2 of the Serbo-Croatian version. It's again reference to an exchange of letters or correspondence between Mr. Prlic and someone named Mahmutcehajic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ILIJA KOZULJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, we're at the end of the time for today, and I simply illustrate to you the process that went into the selection. Mr. Karnavas has absolutely, it appears, to have caught one, that's my error, and we will remove it from the binder, but, sir, you didn't -- in talking about communications between Mostar and Sarajevo, just to be clear, you didn't mean to suggest to the Chamber that there was no communications between Mostar and Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the gentleman never suggested that. He never suggested that yesterday at all, and we'll concede the point that he indicated at times you would send through a courier that would have to go through the tunnel, but there has never been any suggestion and he can pose the question again. But I want to make it clear and I invite the Chamber, any one of you, to point to the transcript where the gentleman did indicate there was no communication. It depends on what period, what time, what type.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I think we need to be -- let's be fair to the gentleman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I was in fact going to intervene because this makes reference to a letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have not studied the document as well as you, no doubt, have. But can you point out where the means of transport of the letter is indicated because it might be by courier. It --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I wasn't communicating -- I wasn't for this purpose, Your Honour, suggesting anything to the contrary. Again, the broad point -- in response to Mr. Karnavas's point, and again I don't think there's any reason for anyone to be short with anyone else, simply I want to be very clear given some of the rather, what I thought, categorical statements by the witness about communication, make it very clear that the Chamber wasn't left with the impression that the statement was in fact broader than apparently Mr. Karnavas has indicated it is. There were -- and I will put to the witness, that there were in fact, and he apparently agrees -- and again I'll be corrected tomorrow if I'm wrong, there were various methods of communication between Sarajevo and Mostar including courier throughout this time-period. That was my point, Your Honour. If that's not disputed, then so much the better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is 7.00. Mr. Scott, you have used two hours so far. You have one hour left. As you know, we shall convene tomorrow at 2.15. Witness, you will be back in this courtroom tomorrow. Have a good evening. I wish a good evening to all of you. Thank you. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of September, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
